newsitem.title: CANADA: Philip, Allwaste agree to merge.
newsitem.headline: Philip, Allwaste agree to merge.

text.p: Philip Environmental Inc and Houston, Texas-based Allwaste Inc said on Thursday they signed a definitive merger agreement whereby each share of Allwaste stock will be exchanged for 0.611 shares of Philip.
Based on the closing price of Philip stock on March 5 the deal values Allwaste at about US$540 million, including the assumption of an estimated US$133 million in debt.

The companies said the merger will create the largest integrated resource recovery and industrial services company in North America, with annualized revenue in excess of US$1.6 billion, about 8,000 employees and 215 operating locations in North America, Europe and South America.
The deal is expected to close in June 1997, subject to shareholder approval of both companies.
Philip and Allwaste said the new company will organize into two major operating divisions: Metals Recovery and Industrial Services.

The Industrial Services division will be comprised of the operations of Allwaste and Philip's existing By-Products Recovery and Environmental Services Groups. The Metals Recovery division will encompass all of Philip's steel, copper and aluminium processing and mill services activities.

"This is a classic opportunity for two companies with limited overlap of customers and an array of complementary services and a specialized industry focus to combine forces," said Philip President and Chief Executive Allen Fracassi.
Allwaste President and Chief Executive Robert Chiste said the companies are a perfect fit.
"Allwaste's strength in industrial services and distribution is supported by Philip's technology leadership and operating strength in the recovery and reuse of industrial by-products," Chiste said.
"We view this as a definitive value-adding event for both companies' stockholders," he added.
